title: Prohibition-era drinking on the road and now
summary: Riddick describes quarts of white lightning at dances and says he seldom drinks now.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: How about on the road if you wanted to drink? And this was during Prohibition. Was it hard to find a drink?

Very much so until you got to where you were playing. And when you started to play that night, as a general rule, the guy that ran the dance brought you a quart of whiskey. And it would knock your head off. Sometimes 110 proof alcohol. Call it white lightning or mountain dew. It's all according to where you were. Up in Tennessee, they called it mountain dew. Mississippi, they called it white lightning. Sometimes we'd be on the road and drinking out of a fruit jar. I got a scar across the bridge of my nose now from going over a bump. Today I seldom have to ever take a drink. I have had a... Let me see. Yes, I have. Since you all were here, I drank one night at a friend of mine who had a party and retired. And he went into retirement. And I had a few drinks there. I got home under my own steam. However, Ellen drove the car home.
And that's the only drink that I've had since you all were here.
And how long ago has it been since you were here? Now, three weeks or something? It was the 14th of July. So it's been a couple of weeks. A couple of weeks. Oh, Lord.
And before that, I hadn't had a drink. I don't remember when.
